This document shall be an integral part of all Employee Contracts. Scope ELCA Information Technology (Vietnam) Limited

Policy 1 Purpose, scope and users The purpose of this document is to define clear rules for the use of information assets and information systems in ELCA Information Technology (Vietnam), Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "ELCA") This document is applied to the entire scope of the Information Security Management System (ISMS), i.e. to all information assets and information systems used within the ISMS scope. Users of this document are all employees of ELCA. 2 Acceptable use of information assets Definitions Information asset: Piece of data that have a value to ELCA. The organization will suffer an adverse impact if: − An information asset is disclosed to unauthorized people − An information asset is modified without authorization − An information asset is lost or destroyed − Access to an information asset is interrupted Information system: Includes all servers and clients, network infrastructure, system and application software, other computer subsystems and components which are owned or used by the organization or which are under the organization's responsibility. The use of an information system also includes the use of all internal or external services, such as Internet access, e-mail, externally hosted services, etc. Asset owner: Person responsible for an information asset or information system. Preamble Users have to be aware of the following facts: − The IT resources and Internet services are put at disposal by ELCA and are to be considered as work tools and to be taken good care of. − ELCA employees are not supposed to make any operations that could have harmful consequences on internal or external information assets and systems, nor on internal or external ELCA relations. − The security rules and recommendations issued by the IT Security Officer are to be applied. − Employees’ acts and behaviour toward information assets and systems may damage ELCA’s image, financial health and productivity, engender legal consequences and even affect people’s health in certain circumstances. Responsibility for assets Each information system has an owner designated in the Inventory of assets. Information systems include IT equipment which is provided by ELCA to employees for the accomplishment of their duties (e.g., personal computers, laptops, screens, external hard disk drives, flash memory drives, etc.), other shared corporate assets (e.g., printers, IT services), as well as all assets an employee may be responsible for due to his/her role. The information system owner is responsible for the confidentiality, integrity and availability of information in the system in question. Processing of assets It is prohibited to use resources in a manner that unnecessarily takes up capacity, weakens the performance of the information system or poses a security threat. Employees must not encroach, disrupt or otherwise interfere with access to or use of ELCA’s information assets and systems. For the avoidance of doubt, without express permission, users must not give away information or send bulk unsolicited email. In addition, users must not engage in other activities that damage, vandalize or otherwise compromise the integrity of ELCA’s information assets or information systems. Consequently, installing non-adapted or potentially dangerous (i.e., containing malicious code) software is forbidden. When working at a client’s, employees should respect the rules stated in the present document or the equivalent ones stated by the client. By adopting a responsible behaviour with regards to information security, employees contribute to the improvement of ELCA’s image. 2.4.1 Respect of the security requirements for information assets When processing information assets (e.g., view, store, copy, exchange, modify, delete, etc.), employees must take into account the applicable security requirements, as stated in the Information Classification document. 2.4.2 Respect of the copyright Users must not make unauthorized copies of software owned by the organization, except in cases permitted by law, by the owner or the IT Security Officer. Users must not copy software or other original materials from other sources and are liable for all consequences that could arise under the intellectual property law. 2.4.3 Respect of the criminal law Users must respect the criminal law and consequently commit to not consulting on Internet, not storing on their computer or not diffusing by their electronic mail or any other electronic means documents which undermine the dignity of the person, present a pornographic character, incite racial hatred, or justify crime or violence. Taking assets off-site When taking information systems off-site, appropriate measures shall be taken in order to ensure the integrity, confidentiality and availability of information assets stored or transported by those systems. As long as said systems are outside the organization, they have to be controlled by the person who was granted permission for their removal. Use of removable media Removable media (e.g., external hard disk drives, flash memory drives) must only be used for legitimate business purpose and the information stored on such devices be removed as soon as they are no longer needed. Only removable media provided by ELCA’s ITS department must be used. Return of assets upon termination of contract Upon termination of an employment contract or other contract on the basis of which information assets and systems are used, the user must return all such information assets and systems to ELCA or corresponding parties. Backup procedure Users are responsible for the back-up of their local files on ELCA’s file hosting service. Malware protection Personal computers provided to ELCA’s employees run an antivirus software configured according to good practices. Users shall not try to impair the proper functioning of the software. They shall notify ELCA’s service desk promptly if they identify a malfunction of the malware protection tool. Authorizations for information assets use Users of the information systems may only access those information assets for which they have been explicitly authorized by the asset owner. Employees may use the information assets only for the purposes for which they have been authorized, i.e., for which they have been granted access rights. Users must not take part in activities which may be used to bypass information system security controls. User account responsibilities The user must not, directly or indirectly, allow another person to use his/her access credentials (e.g., username, password) and must not use another person’s credentials. The use of group usernames is forbidden. The owner of a user account is responsible for all accesses and transactions performed through this user account. Password responsibilities Users must apply good security practices when selecting and using passwords: − Passwords must not be disclosed to other persons, including management and system administrators − Passwords must not be written down, unless a secure method has been approved by the IT Security Officer − User-generated passwords must not be distributed through any channel (using oral, written or electronic distribution, etc.) at the exception of initial temporary passwords − Passwords must be changed if there are indications that the passwords or the system may have been compromised – in that case a security incident must be reported following the incident management process. − Strong passwords must be selected. A strong password characterizes as follows: it cannot be easily guessed, nor easily brute-forced. In order not to be guessable: • A password must not be a dictionary word, dialectal or jargon word from any language, or any of these words written backwards • A password must not be based on personal data (e.g. date of birth, address, name of family member, animal, etc.) • A former password must not be reused or incremented In order not to be brute-forceable: • A password must be long enough (12 characters is considered as a reasonable minimum length) • A password must contain alphabetical, numeric, uppercase, lowercase and special characters − Password must be changed at first log-on to a system. − Passwords must not be stored in an automated log-on system (e.g., macro or browser). − Passwords used for private purposes must not be used for business purposes. Clear desk and clear screen policy Sensitive or critical business information should be locked away (ideally in a fire-resistant safe or cabinet) when not in use, especially when the office is vacated and unlocked (See Critical Information Assets Profile document to identify information with confidentiality requirements). Personal computers and computer terminals are not to be left logged on when unattended and must be locked by password-protected screen savers. They should be shut down at the end of the working day. Sensitive information, when printed, is to be cleared from printers immediately. POL-LE-006 Acceptable use of assets Page 7 / 12 © ELCA Information Technology (Vietnam), Ltd. Internet use Internet browsing is authorized for private use under the employee's sole responsibility, insofar as such use remains reasonable and compatible with the employee's workload. Such use must not compromise the security or computing load of the company's IT network. Employees shall consequently demonstrate the diligence appropriate under the circumstances so as to avoid introducing malicious code into the system through their web browsing activity. The IT Security Officer may block access to some Internet pages for individual users, groups of users or all employees at the organization. If access to some web pages is blocked, the user may submit a written request to IT Security Officer for authorization to access such pages. The user must not try to bypass such restriction autonomously. Employees must regard information received through unverified websites as unreliable. Such information may be used for business purposes only after its authenticity and correctness have been verified. Employees must not use their professional email address to subscribe to newsletters, communicate on forums, blogs or websites which have no link with their professional activity. Employees shall not install additional resources (software or hardware), download any program or other information on the computer provided to them, unless it meets ELCA's needs. Additional resources must be installed from trustworthy sources. In case of doubt, the ELCA IT Security Officer must be consulted. Access to pornographic sites, sites inciting racial hatred, sites constituting an apology from crime and violence, or sites in any other way of a criminal nature is strictly prohibited. The same is true with regard to use of the mailbox to transmit, print or save documents of the same type. Employees are responsible for the consequences arising from unauthorized or inappropriate use of internet and subject to the sanctions provided for in ELCA's Internal Labour Regulations. Use of information exchange means Information exchange means include electronic mail, instant messaging, file transfer platforms, collaboration platforms, telephone calls, text/video messages, portable media, forums and social networks. It is forbidden to send materials with disturbing, unpleasant, sexually explicit, rude, slanderous or any other unacceptable or illegal content. Users must not send spam messages to persons with whom no business relationship has been established or to persons who did not require such information. Should employees receive phishing attack e-mails, they must inform the IT Security Officer. Employees must unambiguously distinguish their private communications from their professional ones. In this regard, they shall not use any ELCA related information exchange means (e.g., ELCA email address and electronic signature, ELCA removable media, etc.) for private use. When exchanging information, employees must use appropriate technical means to ensure that security requirements for the given information asset type are respected, as set in the Critical Information Assets Profile document. In particular, information with confidentiality requirements shall not be disclosed in private communications (e.g., on social networks). Mobile computing 2.16.1 Introduction Mobile computing equipment includes all kinds of portable computers, mobile phones, smart phones, memory cards and other mobile equipment used for storage, processing and transferring of data. 2.16.2 Basic rules Special care should be taken when mobile computing equipment is placed in cars or other forms of transportation, public spaces, hotel rooms, meeting places, conference centres, and other unprotected areas outside the organization's premises. The person taking mobile computing equipment off-premises must follow these rules: − Mobile computing equipment must not be left unattended and, if possible, should be physically locked away − When using mobile computing equipment in public places, employees must take care that data cannot be read by unauthorized persons − If existing security mechanisms such as security patching or protection against malware are not operational, employees must notify the Service Desk without any delay − Remote connection to ELCA resources is performed using the ELCA VPN exclusively Externally hosted services Employees are not allowed to use external hosted services for the processing of information assets (e.g., software development/testing, service hosting, data storage) without explicit authorization from the Head of ITS. Remote working Remote working means that information and communication equipment is used to enable employees to perform their work outside the organization. Remote working is governed by ELCA's Work From Home Policy. Mobile computing equipment used for remote working must be protected as specified in the previous section. Employees shall prevent unauthorized accesses by persons living or working on the location where the remote working activity is performed. This includes applying rules specified in section 2.13 Clear desk and clear screen policy. POL-LE-006 Acceptable use of assets Page 9 / 12 © ELCA Information Technology (Vietnam), Ltd. Monitoring the use of information and communication systems All data which is created, stored, sent or received through the information system or other organization's communication systems, including various applications, e-mail, Internet, etc., whether it is personal or not, is considered the ownership of ELCA. Employees agree that persons from the organization who have a legitimate right to access may process all such data, and that processing by such persons will not be considered a violation of the users' privacy. The organization may use specialized tools for the purpose of identifying and blocking forbidden methods of communication and filtering forbidden content. Reporting of incidents Employees confronted to a system weakness, information security incident or incident suspicion must report it as specified in the Incident Management Procedure. 3 Controls and sanctions Controls and sanctions are governed by ELCA's Internal Labour Regulations. 4 Validity and document management st This document is valid as of 1 January 2022.
